title: First live big bands: Ellington outside the Elks, Jo Jones at the Masonic Temple
summary: He first heard Duke from outside the Elks Hall and sat in as a drummer with Jo Jones in J.T. Watley's band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What was your first contact that you can remember with the name bands in terms of listening, not performing?

Oh, listening. Well, that was in Birmingham. At the time, well, it was no contact. Just listening. That was with Duke Ellington.
But, my contact when I got to 'Bama State, then I had a chance to meet them.
All right. Another way then. When did you first hear live performances by any of the big bands that you were mentioning?
It was in Birmingham
when I was, when I was a kid. Like I said, I wasn't inside. Unless, you want me to go inside. I was outside listening, at Duke.
Outside of where?
At the Elks Hall there in Birmingham, Alabama.
Right.
I wasn't old enough to get in. So, that's the first live, live I remember hearing.
Then, they had a Masonic Temple in Birmingham. By that time, I think I was old enough then. Remember Jo Jones?
Yes.

He was playing there. Well, he was playing in a band there with J.T. Watley. So, I asked him to let me play, sit down and play in his place. I had a little nerve, you know. Now, on them drums he was playing, I want to sit down in a big band. That's where I first had a contact to sit in a big band and play. So, Jo Jones never forgot that. We always knew each other from that for
And that was in Birmingham?
That was in Birmingham.
Okay. And, that was as a drummer?
As a drummer.
Did you ever sit in as a trumpet player in any of these bands during that time because I know you didn't start playing trumpet until a little later.
No. I didn't sit in with them as a trumpet player.
All of that came later.
Came later.
At 'Bama State.
Right.

So, except for the Elks Club and other places like this, there weren't many night club or concert hall type places where you would have been able to go and hear live performances by the travelling bands?
No, there wasn't.
So, the rest of it you would hear on the radio primarily?
That's right.
